readout_other: near-threshold visual object recognition and categorisation task; signal detection d' and criterion
direction_notes: 70% duty cycle to VA thalamus increased recognition sensitivity d'; 70% duty cycle to all four regions decreased categorisation accuracy of real images; 5% duty cycle shifted criterion c (more conservative) for VA and VP.
safety_notes: Simulated maximal temperature rise 0.23 +/- 0.04 C; transducer noise awareness recorded (93% at 5% DC, 52% at 70% DC) and included as covariate.

exposures.label: LIFU to four left thalamic regions (VA, VP, DA, DP) at 70% or 5% duty cycle

target.label: four regions of the left thalamus, including the VA, VP, DA, and DP thalamus

timing.protocol_description: Pulse repetition frequency 10 Hz (100 ms period), duty cycle 70% or 5% (pulse width 70 or 5 ms), 30 s sonication alternating with 30 s off, 12 sonications per block; four LIFU-ON blocks, one per thalamic region in pseudorandomised order, one duty cycle per participant.

flags.reason: Text lists 'pulse duration: 100 ms', which matches the 10 Hz period, and separately 'pulse width of 70 and 5 ms'; the pulse width values were recorded as pulse duration (burst rule resolved from the paper's own pulse-width statement).

Derated (FDA method, 0.3 dB/cm/MHz) values recorded as in_situ; the paper also gives simulated in-brain pressure of 72.6 and 258.2 kPa (70% and 5% DC) from BabelBrain, not recorded here. Non-derated incident values placed in unspecified_domain because the paper does not name the medium.
60 enrolled and randomised; 54 analysed (27 per group). Enrolled number recorded.
Four thalamic subregions (VA, VP, DA, DP) are listed as one exposure; the authors' VA is not the classical VA nucleus.
Two duty cycles given to two separate groups; list order [70,5] matches pressure and intensity lists.
Transducer noise awareness was surveyed and used as a covariate; no masking or sham.
